Here’s a hypothetical client profile and a set of 100 distinct things they might say during a therapy session.

### Backstory
The client is **Maya**, a 34-year-old high school literature teacher living in a mid-sized city. She grew up in a household where emotions were rarely discussed openly; her father was affectionate but unpredictable, and her mother tended to dismiss distress by saying things like “just stay busy” or “don’t make a big deal out of it.” Maya was the oldest child and became the “responsible one” early on, often caring for her younger brother when her parents argued.

In college, Maya excelled academically but struggled socially, often worrying that others found her awkward or boring. She learned to over-prepare, people-please, and hide her anxiety behind competence. After graduating, she became a teacher because she loved books and wanted to make a difference, but the job has become increasingly overwhelming. In the past two years, a breakup, the death of her grandmother, and mounting financial stress have intensified her depression and anxiety. She’s been sleeping poorly, feeling detached from her friends, and constantly worried she’s failing at work. She often feels guilty for not being “strong enough,” even though she continues to function externally.

---

### 100 statements Maya may say to her therapist

1. “I feel like I’m barely holding myself together most days.”
2. “I’m exhausted all the time, even when I haven’t done much.”
3. “I keep waiting to feel better, but it never really happens.”
4. “My mind won’t shut off, especially at night.”
5. “I overthink every conversation I have.”
6. “I’m scared people at work can tell I’m struggling.”
7. “I used to be so much more capable than this.”
8. “Everything feels like a chore lately.”
9. “I can’t remember the last time I felt genuinely calm.”
10. “I keep thinking I’m disappointing everyone.”
11. “Even small tasks feel strangely overwhelming.”
12. “I’ve been avoiding texts because I don’t have the energy to reply.”
13. “I feel guilty for being sad when other people have bigger problems.”
14. “I don’t feel like myself anymore.”
15. “I’m functioning, but only barely.”
16. “I wake up already anxious before I’ve even opened my eyes.”
17. “I keep replaying mistakes in my head.”
18. “It’s like my brain is stuck in alarm mode.”
19. “I worry that if I stop moving, I’ll completely fall apart.”
20. “I don’t know how to relax without feeling guilty.”
21. “I’m afraid I’m becoming a burden to the people around me.”
22. “I smile a lot, but it doesn’t feel real.”
23. “I’ve been eating because I’m stressed, then feeling bad about that too.”
24. “Sometimes I just sit in my car before going inside because I can’t face the day.”
25. “I feel disconnected from everyone, even when I’m with them.”
26. “I miss the version of me that used to enjoy things.”
27. “I keep telling myself to tough it out, but I’m tired of doing that.”
28. “I feel ashamed that I need help.”
29. “I don’t trust my own judgment when I’m anxious.”
30. “I’m worried that if I make one mistake, everything will unravel.”
31. “I can’t stop imagining worst-case scenarios.”
32. “My chest feels tight a lot of the time.”
33. “I’m always bracing for something bad to happen.”
34. “I’ve started avoiding things I used to handle easily.”
35. “I feel like I’m failing at being an adult.”
36. “Some mornings it feels impossible to get out of bed.”
37. “I’ve been crying more than I want anyone to know.”
38. “I’m embarrassed by how much I’m struggling.”
39. “I keep comparing myself to everyone else and coming up short.”
40. “I’m afraid I’ll never feel like myself again.”
41. “I’ve gotten very good at pretending I’m okay.”
42. “When people ask how I’m doing, I don’t know what to say.”
43. “I’m scared this is just who I am now.”
44. “I feel numb in ways I can’t really explain.”
45. “I’m lonely, even when I’m surrounded by people.”
46. “I don’t know how to ask for support without feeling weak.”
47. “I’m constantly second-guessing myself.”
48. “It takes so much effort to seem normal.”
49. “I feel like I’m behind in life.”
50. “I used to be proud of how dependable I was, and now I just feel broken.”
51. “My thoughts get so loud that I can’t focus on anything else.”
52. “I’ve been forgetting simple things, and that scares me.”
53. “I feel like I’m carrying too much, but I don’t know how to put it down.”
54. “I can’t tell whether I’m anxious, depressed, or just burnt out.”
55. “I keep thinking I should be stronger than this.”
56. “I’m afraid my students can sense I’m not okay.”
57. “I feel like I’m performing my life instead of living it.”
58. “I don’t have much hope when I think about the future.”
59. “I’m so tired of being scared all the time.”
60. “I avoid making decisions because I’m terrified of choosing wrong.”
61. “I feel trapped by my own thoughts.”
62. “I miss feeling excited about anything.”
63. “I’ve been isolating because it’s easier than explaining myself.”
64. “I’m afraid people will judge me if they knew how bad it is.”
65. “I don’t recognize the person I’ve become lately.”
66. “I feel like I’m always one bad day away from collapsing.”
67. “I keep telling myself I’m fine, but I don’t think I believe it.”
68. “I’m scared to slow down because I might have to feel everything.”
69. “I’ve been waking up in the middle of the night with my heart racing.”
70. “I don’t feel hopeful in the way I used to.”
71. “I’m worried I’m not enough, no matter how hard I try.”
72. “It feels impossible to quiet my inner critic.”
73. “I want relief, but I don’t know what that would even look like.”
74. “I’m ashamed of how much reassurance I need.”
75. “I feel like I’m always apologizing for existing.”
76. “I’ve been snapping at people, and then I feel terrible about it.”
77. “I’m scared I’m going to lose my job if this keeps going.”
78. “I can’t concentrate long enough to finish basic things.”
79. “I feel emotionally fragile all the time.”
80. “I’m afraid to be alone with my thoughts.”
81. “I don’t know how much longer I can keep pretending everything is normal.”
82. “Sometimes I think everyone would be better off if I were less of a problem.”
83. “I hate how much space this takes up in my life.”
84. “I feel like I’m watching my life happen from a distance.”
85. “I’m worried I’ve become too dependent on other people’s approval.”
86. “I keep expecting myself to bounce back, but I don’t.”
87. “I’m not sure what I need anymore.”
88. “I feel ashamed that simple things feel so hard.”
89. “I’m scared that if I let myself rest, I’ll never get back up.”
90. “I don’t know how to be kind to myself.”
91. “I feel like I’m carrying grief I never properly dealt with.”
92. “I miss my grandmother, and I think I’ve been avoiding that loss.”
93. “I keep thinking about the breakup like it was proof I’m unlovable.”
94. “I’m afraid I’m too much for people.”
95. “I’m also afraid I’m not enough.”
96. “I don’t know how to trust that things can improve.”
97. “I’m tired of living in my head.”
98. “I want to feel safe in my own life again.”
99. “I think I need help, but asking for it feels hard.”
100. “I’m here because I don’t want to keep doing this alone.”

If you want, I can also turn these into:
- a **more realistic therapist-client dialogue**,
- a version that sounds **more emotionally raw**, or
- a version tailored to a **different backstory**.
